title: Keto Caramel Pecan Swirl Cupcakes
shortDescription: Almond flour cupcakes with a caramel swirl frosting, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a caramel pecan pie in cake form, but they stay low carb. I use almond and coconut flour for a soft. Moist crumb that holds up well to the frosting The swirl on top is a simple butter frosting with sugar-free caramel folded through it, so you get ribbons of caramel in every bite. A drizzle of extra caramel sauce and chopped pecans finish the top I tested this batch three times in my own kitchen to get the crumb right. Almond flour alone made them too dense, so coconut flour helps lighten things up. This is a great keto treat for fall gatherings or anytime you want a caramel fix without the sugar crash.
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk almond flour, coconut flour, erythritol, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, mix melted butter, eggs, heavy cream, vanilla, and caramel extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir until just combined, no dry streaks.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
Beat softened butter until fluffy, about 2 minutes. Add powdered erythritol and heavy cream, beat until smooth.
Fold 1/4 cup sugar-free caramel sauce into the frosting gently, leaving visible swirls rather than mixing fully.
Once cupcakes are fully cool, pipe the caramel swirl frosting on top.
Drizzle with the remaining caramel sauce and sprinkle chopped pecans over each cupcake.
tips: Cool cupcakes all the way before frosting or the butter frosting will slide right off.
Warm the caramel sauce slightly before folding it in, so it swirls instead of clumping.
Toast the pecans in a dry pan for 3 minutes for a deeper, nuttier crunch on top.
If your caramel sauce is thin, chill it 10 minutes before drizzling for cleaner lines.

faq.question: What sugar-free caramel sauce works best for this recipe?
faq.answer: I use a store-bought allulose or monk fruit caramel sauce, or a homemade one made with butter, cream, and allulose. Both fold into frosting and drizzle well without seizing.

faq.question: Can I use a different keto sweetener in the frosting?
faq.answer: Yes, powdered monk fruit blend works as a swap for erythritol in the frosting. Keep the amount the same for the right texture.

faq.question: Why did my cupcakes turn out dense?
faq.answer: Dense cupcakes usually mean the batter was overmixed or the coconut flour was measured too heavy. Spoon and level the coconut flour instead of scooping it.

faq.question: Can I make these nut-free?
faq.answer: Swap the almond flour for sunflower seed flour at the same amount and skip the pecans on top. The cake texture stays close to the original.

conclusion: These caramel pecan cupcakes prove keto baking can still feel like dessert, not a compromise. Keep a batch in the fridge for a quick low carb treat all week.
